newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco talks still hinge on punitive damages - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco talks still hinge on punitive damages - WSJ.

text.p: If negotiators in tobacco settlement talks are unable to reach an agreement on a provision concerning immunity from punitive damages for cigarette makers, they may leave the matter unresolved, the Wall Street Journal said.
In Monday's electronic edition, the Journal said that the dispute may mean that any settlement agreement presented to the White House could come with some holes.
Meanwhile, B.A.T Industries Plc Chief Executive Martin Broughton, in New York Friday for a meeting at Philip Morris Co's headquarters, backed off his previous opposition to a deal.

However, he said he did not believe the industry should go to the White House until the issue of punitive damages is resolved, sources told the Journal. And Philip Morris and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp apparently share Broughton's view, the newspaper said.
"If the industry doesn't get this assurance, the deal is in trouble," one unnamed source in the industry said. "This may be what decides if the deal gets done any time soon."
